_comment: This project's OWN gate cases. The hub's test-gates.ps1 proves the mechanism against a synthetic
fixture and knows nothing about this project; these prove THIS project's rules. Run them with
The flash cases exist because this repo's output goes onto a real controller: flashing reboots
it, and an unrequested flash is a hardware action taken on my own initiative. Building is the
turn's verification and must never be caught by the same rule - hence the allow cases.

cases.name: flashing on my own initiative is blocked
cases.prompt: fix the hang watchdog grace period

cases.name: the loader CLI is the same rule by another name
cases.prompt: fix the hang watchdog grace period

cases.name: flashing asked for in this turn is allowed
cases.prompt: build it and flash the teensy so I can test

cases.name: the ordinary verification build is never touched
cases.prompt: fix the hang watchdog grace period

cases.name: the teensy40 build is never touched either
cases.prompt: fix the hang watchdog grace period

cases.name: full-path pio (not on PATH on Windows) is still caught when uploading
cases.prompt: fix the hang watchdog grace period

cases.name: full-path pio building is still allowed
cases.prompt: fix the hang watchdog grace period

cases.name: platformio, the long name, is caught when uploading
cases.prompt: fix the hang watchdog grace period

cases.name: platformio building is allowed
cases.prompt: fix the hang watchdog grace period

cases.name: a commit MESSAGE quoting the upload form is prose, not a flash
cases.command:
git commit -m @'
turn-gate: match platformio too

The same gap let platformio run -t upload through the flash gate.
'@

cases.name: verify: the Windows full-path exe form counts
verify: the posix venv path counts
verify: cleaning is NOT a verification
verify: cleaning under the long name is NOT one either
verify: an upload builds first, so it counts as one
